description: Two students, one shared braincell, and big cosmic ambitions.
summary:
Flame in Freefall is a source-grounded decision-support platform built on NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion archive.

We unified all 19 NASA PSI fire investigations - 1,810 experimental runs and 6,199 normalized measurements across Fire Prevention, Detection, and Suppression - into one verified SQLite database and Streamlit workspace. Users can filter raw experiments, rank tests by mission atmosphere, and evaluate materials. When no exact experimental match exists, a locally trained ML model predicts missing parameters within its validated applicability domain, while strict guardrails block unsafe extrapolation and unverified AI claims.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Flame in Freefall turns 19 fragmented NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion investigations into a unified, SI-normalized SQLite database (1,810 experimental runs, 6,199 physical measurements, and 68 SHA-256-tracked source files) paired with an interactive four-workspace application:

  1. Overview: Visualizes the experimental landscape across oxygen concentration, cabin pressure, ventilation airflow, fuel categories, and gravity regimes (0g vs. 1g).
  2. Database Explorer: Lets users filter every recorded run and sensor measurement by investigation, material, gravity, and combustion outcome, and upload custom CSV/XLSX lab files in-session to compare their own data against NASA records.
  3. Research Discovery (Ranking): Uses a deterministic scoring model (0–100) to rank NASA investigations by relevance to specific mission atmospheres (ISS, Lunar Base, Mars Habitat, Deep Space) across three fire-safety pillars: Prevention, Detection, and Suppression.
    • Exact Retrieval (OBSERVED): Returns verified experimental measurements stratified by apparatus and measurement definition.
    • Local ML Fallback (ML_PREDICTED / INTERPOLATED): When exact experimental points do not exist in the archive, trained local machine learning surrogate models estimate outcomes with uncertainty intervals inside validated feature bounds.
    • Source-Grounded AI Synthesis: Optionally uses Google Gemini to summarize findings while citing exact PSI record IDs and document locators.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Faster Engineering Decisions: Eliminates hours of manual searching across disparate NASA spreadsheets, text logs, and PDF reports by normalizing all records into standard SI units with direct links to original DOIs and files.
  • Safer Deep-Space Habitats: Highlights counterintuitive microgravity fire behavior—such as solid fuels sustaining combustion down to 13.5% O2O_2O2​ in 0g0g0g (BASS-II) compared to ~15.4–19% O2O_2O2​ in 1g1g1g, and microgravity smoke particles shifting to 80–179 nm (SAME / SAME-R).
  • Exposing the Partial-Gravity Gap: Reveals that all 19 PSI combustion datasets cover 0g and 1g, with zero sustained flame tests at Lunar (1/6g1/6g1/6g) or Martian (3/8g3/8g3/8g) gravity, helping mission planners bracket risk within the 0g–1g corridor for Artemis Lunar Base atmospheres (≥30% O2\ge 30\%\ O_2≥30% O2​, ≤10.2 psi\le 10.2\text{ psi}≤10.2 psi).
  • Earth Applications: Provides clean baseline data (without buoyant convection distortion) for designing false-alarm-resistant optical smoke detectors, cleaner fuel combustion engines, and fire protection in submarines, mines, and cleanrooms.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

  • Language: Python
  • Web Interface & Visualization: Streamlit, Plotly, Matplotlib
  • Database & Data Pipeline: SQLite (sqlite3), Pandas, NumPy, Pydantic, Pint, OpenPyXL, PyPDF
  • Machine Learning & AI: Scikit-Learn and SciPy (local regression/surrogate models with applicability domain checks and prediction intervals), Google Gemini API (google-genai SDK) for optional source-cited interpretation
  • Testing & Verification: Pytest and Streamlit AppTest

How the Project Is Creative & Factors Considered

  • Protocol-Stratified Integrity (No Blending of Incompatible Data): A major challenge in NASA's archive is that different investigations measure the "same" property using incompatible methods (e.g., geometric vs. mass mean smoke diameter, or nominal vs. sensor-measured cabin pressure). Our engine strictly separates these definitions so charts and answers never mix incompatible protocols.
  • Hybrid Database + Local ML with Strict Guardrails: Instead of relying on an LLM to guess numbers, we trained local ML models on verified PSI experimental series and enforced strict domain boundaries. Models that do not meet cross-validation reliability thresholds are automatically withheld, and out-of-domain queries return an explicit scientific abstention rather than a hallucinated answer.
  • Relevance vs. Safety Certification: Our team deliberately separated research relevance from material safety certification—ensuring users know which NASA experiments match their mission conditions without falsely claiming a material is certified safe for untested partial-gravity environments.
